label: early-position "m" (and k/b/p) input in the original phase
explanation: Fires almost only in the original phase (97% of mass) at very early positions t=1..3 (t=2 alone is 78% of mass), never at t=0 and almost never in the copy phase. Token identity matters a lot: input m holds 66% of the mass, and m at t=2 is active 98% of the time with the largest activations (top examples are all m at t=2, e.g. x m m or r d m). m at t=1 fires weakly (about 0.1 of max); m at t=3 fires less reliably. Secondary tokens k, b, p (and weaker q, a) fire at t=2 only about 40% of the time, and the earlier tokens modulate this (prior r, x, d, m, 0, u, w raise the rate) in ways a simple rule does not capture. A small tail fires on <DEL> when L=3 (t=3). It does not fire on most other letters, on digits, or at later original positions (t>=4). Predicate dev F1 0.67, mass recall 0.83.
